subject: Request: temporary hot-lane priority slice for BlueHarvest pilot
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary hot-lane priority slice for BlueHarvest pilot

Team —

BlueHarvest is kicking off their enterprise pilot next Tuesday (May 4) and just shared a refined traffic forecast that bumps 95th p95 token QPS for their streaming endpoint by ~3x during peak business hours. They’ve requested a short-lived "hot-lane" (priority slice) to guarantee latency SLOs while they run the pilot (2-week window, May 4–May 17).

Ask: can we provision a temporary priority slice of 8 A100-equivalent slots (or equivalent GPUs/slots per the pool plan) with an autoscale exception to 12 slots for short spikes (max 2hr/day)?

Why: BlueHarvest is sensitive to tail latency; if we can’t promise the hot-lane they’ve indicated they will pause the pilot and push to another vendor. This is an expansion opportunity and we want to keep the pilot running.

Proposed guardrails:
- Timebox: 2027-05-04 00:00 PST through 2027-05-17 23:59 PST
- Hard cap: 12 slots absolute max; automated throttling beyond 10 unless we manually approve
- Telemetry: enable token-level latency tracing and a temporary dashboard (attached)
- Rollback: automatic removal after window; any overage billed to BlueHarvest (marginal rate)

Attached: pilot_traffic_forecast.csv (traffic by hour), sla_telemetry_dashboard.png. I filled the exception form as a draft (exception_request_form.pdf) — can Ops own the formal approval flow?

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pilot_traffic_forecast.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: sla_telemetry_dashboard.png (image)]
[Attachment: exception_request_form.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hot-lane priority slice for BlueHarvest pilot

On Fri, 01 May 2027 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team —
>
> BlueHarvest is kicking off their enterprise pilot next Tuesday ...

Thanks for the context, Soojin. A couple quick operational questions before I sign off:

1) Expected baseline utilization: what percent of the 8-slot slice do they expect to use during off-peak vs peak? The CSV shows aggregated QPS but we need slot-level mapping to verify scheduling impact.
2) Autoscale policy: do we want a soft-autoscale (fast scale up, slow scale down) for this window, or force fixed slice with manual override? Soft autoscale will affect other pool tenants during cold starts.
3) Billing/chargeback: confirm BlueHarvest agrees to cover marginal costs for the 2-week window — internal Finance needs a one-paragraph approval.

If we get the slot-utilization breakdown and confirmation of billing, I can push an exception to the reservation controller and provision the slice on Monday morning (2027-05-03). Also adding INF-8472 to track.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hot-lane priority slice for BlueHarvest pilot

Marcus —

Product perspective: BlueHarvest is running our feature flag rollout that depends on steady <100ms p95 for LIVE streaming use. If we don’t provide a reliable hot-lane they will not be able to evaluate production behavior. I approve the principle of a short priority slice under the following conditions:

- We get the slot-level utilization mapping before Monday 10:00 AM PST.
- Limit autoscale to 2 spikes (up to 12 slots) per day and a max duration of 2 hours per spike. Any more than that requires Ops + Product review.
- Telemetry: enable the new trace-level sampling for their tokens and add a guardrail alert if p95 exceeds 150ms for more than 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets.

Soojin, please cc Finance for the billing confirmation and have BlueHarvest sign the short addendum I attached in Drive (link in thread). Marcus, if you can stage the slice in staging tomorrow and run the smoke tests we can greenlight Monday provisioning.

Kimberly Park
VP Product — Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@blueharvest.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: trial-ops@blueharvest.ai
Date: Sat, 02 May 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hot-lane priority slice for BlueHarvest pilot

Thanks, Soojin and team. BlueHarvest confirms: we accept the 2-week window (May 4–May 17) and agree to the billing terms for marginal capacity. Our expected utilization: baseline 40% of the 8-slot slice off-peak, rising to ~90% during peak hours (11:00–15:00 PST). We will keep trial-ops updated if forecast changes.

We also confirm we are comfortable with the telemetry sampling to help debug tail latency during the pilot. Per Kimberly's note we will sign the addendum by COB Monday, May 3.

— Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Engineering — BlueHarvest Labs

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary hot-lane priority slice for BlueHarvest pilot

Per the thread and the confirmed utilization numbers from BlueHarvest, Ops approved a one-time exception:

- Provisioning: 8-slot priority slice allocated from the enterprise GPU pool on 2027-05-04 03:00 PST
- Autoscale: soft autoscale allowed to 12 slots; enforced limit of 2 spike-events/day and 2 hours/spike
- Telemetry & Alerting: tracing enabled; p95 guardrail alert configured (threshold 150ms, 3 buckets)
- Billing: BlueHarvest to be invoiced for marginal usage; Finance (cc'd separately) will confirm rate

Marcus — please confirm staging smoke test results in INF-8472. Soojin — thanks for driving this; please share the signed addendum when available.

Kimberly Park
VP Product — Redwood Inference
